item.title: ‘I’m heartbroken’: experts dismayed as US loses long-held measles elimination status
item.description:
UNITED STATES—A scientific triumph that quietly shaped a generation, the United States’ measles-elimination status passed away on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Hailed as an unmitigated good and a borderline miracle on its initial appearance, then quickly forgotten, Measles Elimination had seemed to have many more good years ahead of it. Its decline was sudden and dramatic, and it had been feuding with the secretary of health and human services for some time, although he denied having any direct role in its demise. Observers described its death as “senseless,” “utterly senseless,” “an enormous step backward,” and “the kind of thing that makes you lose all hope in human progress.” Measles Elimination arrived in 2000 as the proud work of scientists and doctors and public messaging. item.title: Ukraine: Kyiv targets Krasnodar refineries after felling Kerch bridge
item.description:
A picture taken on July 17, 2023, shows a Russian warship sailing near the Kerch bridge, which links the Russian mainland to Crimea, following an attack claimed by Ukrainian forces. —STRINGER––AFP/Getty Images An overnight Ukrainian missile attack has severely damaged the vital Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia, delivering a symbolic blow to Russian President Vladimir Putin ahead of a summit in Asia where he is expected to meet President Donald Trump . The road and rail bridge was built after Russia invaded and annexed the Crimean peninsula in 2014 and connects Crimea to Russia's southern Krasnodar region. Ukrainian officials shared videos on social media that appeared to show a missile strike on the bridge and an entire section of the structure collapsing. item.title: Get Government Out of Air Traffic Control
item.description:
The tottering nature of the U.S. air traffic control (ATC) system was highlighted again last week when the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a "ground stop," halting flights across the country because of technical issues. The government is attributing the problem to equipment problems, which is believable for a long-obsolete, government-run system undergoing piecemeal modernization. In fact, the FAA had been warned that disruptions were likely. After repeated problems, sometimes caused by government shutdowns, it's time to point out once more that the U.S. should follow the lead of other countries and strip politicians of responsibility for something as important as air traffic control. item.title: Banks, flights, email… What’s behind series of US tech outages?
item.description:
US Secretary of State Marco insisted Wednesday that authorities have found "zero evidence" that recent outages across tech platforms are related to one another or due to the work of "nefarious actors." It follows multiple disruptions of everything from US air traffic operations to Microsoft email and messaging to banking and mobile pay. France 24’s Philip Turle takes a closer look.
